_comment: Scenario-staged routing demo beside impassable terrain: a brittle player cavalry unit (60 mounts at morale 0.5) starts just west of the default hill (Rect2(1150, 380, 250, 200)) and holds there until an enemy cavalry charge from its WESTERN flank comes in; it moves out about 80 wu west to meet the charge and, after a long melee, breaks and routs. Both units stand clear of the hill for the whole clip: the router's block is 280 wu wide, so its centre at x=960 keeps its eastern file 50 wu clear of the hill's west face, and the whole scene sits 140 wu west of its pre-backstop staging (router 1100 -> 960, pursuer 930 -> 790, the spawn gap unchanged). On the earlier staging six of the router's men stood inside the hill, and once the soldier terrain backstop held them at the edge the router ended up fighting instead of routing. Measured with a 4-tick dense state dump: the router holds at its spawn through tick 160, is in melee from about tick 316, routs at tick 472, and stays ROUTING to the end of the clip, drifting west away from the hill as its morale recovers. This scenario does NOT show a rout detouring around the hill: the router's flight never meets it. The 'stands and fights when genuinely trapped' case is covered by test_trapped_routing_unit_fights_instead_of_fleeing. No player input needed; the scenario + seed make the clash deterministic. The pursuer's own block deforms during the post-rout gallop (a 4-tick scan reads shape residual up to ~77 wu across ticks 480-640), so the declared checks pin the router's story beats and leave mid-gallop pursuer samples out. Small spawn shifts change the cavalry clash a lot. In 4-tick dense scans, moving the whole scene 20 wu either way, or moving the router 20 wu east (alone, or with the pursuer 40 wu east) each gave the pursuer a facing whipsaw (6 to 16 reversals): its charge glances and it re-charges, swinging its facing by about 100 degrees each time (12 to 116 degrees and back, four times between ticks 168 and 264 on the 20-wu-east scene). Keep the spawn gap and re-run the dense scan before moving either unit.
